thread:
leo: Hey team — hitting a reproducible problem with streaming responses. Long generations (>30s) sometimes arrive as truncated JSON after a transient reconnect. The final event is missing (no finish_reason, no final chunk) and client JSON parser errors out. Repro steps below. Can you help triage?

maria (support): Thanks for the report leo — can you paste the exact raw SSE frames you observed and any response headers? Also: are you using our hosted API or Dedicated?

leo: Hosted. Raw capture: we see multiple `data:` lines then connection dropped, client reconnects and receives a partial `data:` payload that ends mid-object. Example concatenated payload (trimmed):

```
data: {"id":"abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...long text..."},"index":0}]
data: {"id":"abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...continued"},"index":0}],"meta":{"tokens_so_far":482}
```

(then connection closes, no `[DONE]` or `finish_reason` payload). Our SSE parser throws: `unexpected end of JSON input` when it tries to parse the concatenated `data:` buffer.

nina (support-engineer): Thanks — two quick clarifying Qs: 1) does your client attempt to reconnect and resume using any custom headers (e.g., Last-Event-ID or a resume token)? 2) do you see any 4xx/5xx in the immediate response or only connection close?

leo: We do a simple reconnect (no Last-Event-ID). The reconnect gets a 200 but the first chunk is mid-object like above. No 4xx/5xx observed from our client.

ajay (eng-runtime): Pinging runtime infra — this sounds like an edge/proxy or connection middlebox is closing during the final flush. Two possibilities come to mind: a) proxy/LB timeout cut the socket before the server wrote the final `finish` event, or b) the client reconnect logic is reusing the same logical request-id and our streaming runtime doesn't implement resume semantics, so the new connection receives a different generation's partial state.

olivia (sre): I pulled the edge logs for request id matching the time window. I see the following in envoy access logs: `upstream_transport_failure_reason: "connection termination"` and an upstream reset with `reason: reset`. Runtime logs for that request show the model produced tokens up to end but the final flush attempted failed with `write: broken pipe`. Full snippet: 

```
[2026-03-14T18:44:12.320Z] request_id=abc123 stage=generate tokens=489
[2026-03-14T18:44:42.986Z] request_id=abc123 stage=flush err="write: broken pipe"
[2026-03-14T18:44:42.986Z] request_id=abc123 stage=complete final_chunk_sent=false
```
olivia: So server believes final chunk didn't make it to the client. There's also a proxy (cloud edge) close at ~30s in the logs.

maria: That lines up with customers seeing missing final `finish_reason`. How often is this happening for you, leo?

leo: Roughly 1 in 40 long-generation calls (we're using temperature=0.7, max_tokens=1024). We saw it in prod and were able to reproduce in a tighter loop by forcing slightly longer responses.

ajay: Two immediate mitigation suggestions while we investigate infra: 1) set an explicit keepalive/heartbeat from the server every ~10s to prevent proxy idle timeouts, 2) client-side: buffer SSE event fragments and only parse JSON after receiving a complete event (i.e., wait for an empty line separating events or a `[DONE]` sentinel). Also, if you can, switch to non-stream mode for critical calls to avoid partial states.

leo: Buffering helps but we don't control upstream proxies; curious about reconnect behavior — after the disconnect our client issues a new downstream request and sometimes receives a 200 with a mid-object first chunk. Why would the server respond mid-object on a fresh connection?

ajay: Hypothesis: our runtime's continuous-batch / streaming pipeline writes partial chunks to the response stream as they are produced. If the client disconnects then immediately reconnects, the new TCP connection can be routed to a different backend instance that has no context; however, if the edge layer replays buffered bytes from the previous connection (some edge proxies do aggressive buffering), the new connection might receive leftover bytes that represent an incomplete mid-object chunk. That leads to the exact symptom you see.

olivia: Another angle: some load-balancers/edge middleboxes support connection coalescing / fast-retry where they replay the upstream response into the new connection — this can produce a concatenation of bytes that weren't meant to be a self-contained first event. The presence of `write: broken pipe` in runtime logs shows the server definitely didn't finish final event.

nina: For reproducibility, can you run this curl-based capture and attach the raw output? Repro steps:

1) Run: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-large" \
  --no-buffer -o sse_raw.txt
```
2) Interrupt after ~20-35s (ctrl+c) to force a client-side reconnect scenario, then immediately re-run the same curl. Capture both sse_raw.txt files and `tcpdump -w reconnect.pcap` during the test.

leo: Will do and attach logs.

ajay: Engineering action items I'll own: (A) add an explicit final-event flush retry: if an upstream write fails with EPIPE/ECONNRESET, persist the final-chunk to a short-lived durable buffer and attempt to deliver it on a subsequent connection when the same request id is replayed within 10s. (B) add server-side keepalive pings (every 10s) so proxies don't idle-timeout. (C) add tracing headers in responses: `x-rw-stream-seq` so we can correlate partial deliveries.

olivia: SRE action: increase cloud edge idle timeout for streaming routes to 90s and disable aggressive retry/coalescing behavior for these endpoints. We'll test this change in canary tomorrow.

maria: Support action: I'll tell affected customers the temporary workarounds (client buffering, non-stream mode for critical runs) and request the raw captures. I'll also reference this thread to customers reporting similar symptoms so they know we're on it.

leo: Thanks — attaching sse_raw_1.txt and sse_raw_2.txt; here are the raw first/second runs (redacted token):

```
--- run 1 start ---
data: {"id":"abc123","object":"stream","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Once upon a time..."},"index":0}]
data: {"id":"abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...continued part A"},"index":0}]
--- connection closed by peer ---
--- run 2 start ---
data: {"id":"abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...continued part B"},"index":0}],"meta":{"tokens_so_far":512}
```

leo: You can see run2's first event is mid-object and missing closing braces.

ajay: That's perfect repro. Adding this to the high-priority ticket. For completeness, we should also rule out auth/billing: if the token rotates midstream and edge rejected bytes, you'd see a 401/402. Since you saw 200 and server logs show writes reaching runtime, it's not billing/auth.

nina: Posting a short checklist for customers to mitigate while we patch: 
- Buffer SSE event frames and only parse on event boundary.
- If you must reconnect, add a small jitter before reconnecting to avoid racey replay scenarios.
- Use non-stream endpoints for any critical, single-response work.

olivia: I'll follow up with the canary results tomorrow. ajay, can you estimate ETA for the server-side flush-retry change?

ajay: I'll get a PR out in ~48h for the keepalive and tracing headers, flush-retry is trickier (needs durable short-lived buffering) — estimate 7-10 days for an initial safe implementation behind feature flag.

maria: Great — I'll update the customer and mark the case P2. leo, thanks for the detailed repro, that sped this up.

leo: Appreciate the fast triage. One extra note: some clients prefer SSE parsers that can survive partial JSON by concatenating successive `data:` lines until a blank line — we implemented that and it avoids crashes but still sees missing finish_reason. Looking forward to the server-side changes.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-239 (stream-truncate-replay). Assigned: eng-runtime, infra.

ajay: I'll post PR links and milestone updates to this thread once available.

maria: Closing the loop for now; re-open if you hit anything new.

leo: Thanks all!
